unit.why: A single anecdote: while the tzaddik R. David Moshe (rd"m) recites 'Anenu' in public, his only son faints from the crowd and the heat, and he keeps praying without interruption.

stories.start_quote: כתב הרב הגדול מוהר"י הלוי וועבער
stories.summary_en: During the communal recitation of 'Anenu', the crowd presses around R. David Moshe so it can hear his whispered words, and his son R. Israel faints from the crush and the heat; told of it, the tzaddik does not lift his eyes from the selichah, motions for the son to be taken away, and goes on without pause.

quotes: לא הסיב עיניו מהסליחה אף על רגע אחת
tags.why: Communal recitation of selichot / Anenu is the setting.
He is so absorbed in prayer that he does not hear the commotion.
His rapt state cuts him off from his surroundings.

quotes: ומחמת הדוחק והחום נתעלף בנו הרה״ק
tags.why: The tzaddik's only son is a character.
The point of the anecdote is to illustrate the tzaddik's unbroken concentration in prayer.
Only a metaphor for his fiery words, so borderline.

quotes: או בי"ג מדות או בליל יוה״ק
tags.why: The occasion may have been Yom Kippur night; the narrator is unsure.

quotes: וכל הצבור רצו לשמוע דבריו הקדושים
tags.why: The community crowds around him in reverence.
